blocker.summary: r478 (Piste A of the approved plan) added a static primitive_type trace to r476's existing diagnostic in native_vulkan_backend.cpp and confirmed the 3 remaining vertex-shader rejections in the native probe are genuinely uncaptured primitive_type states, not a PM4 decode bug. Direct registry query (via materialize_pinned_shader_capsule.parse_capsule on the 320-entry native/fixtures/pinned-shader-registry.v1.bin) found: two vertex shaders (09dd1c7cddae1141, 57b8e5f14b93cff4) already exist in the registry but each only under the OPPOSITE rect_strip_expand value the native probe's real draw needs (a clean, symmetric inversion); a third (4dd456c4ea0923c1) is absent under any modification at all. Reading native_xenos.cpp confirmed primitive_type is extracted uniformly per-draw (payload[N] & 0x3F from VGT_DRAW_INITIATOR) with no shader-dependent logic -- no plausible mechanism for a shader-specific inversion, so this is not a decode bug. Consistent with generic UI vertex shaders reused across different draw contexts by the game itself. No new oracle capture was run this cycle per explicit user instruction (static trace first). Named for r479: a user decision is needed -- covering these three gaps needs a NEW sealed oracle route that reaches the exact screen the native zero-input probe traverses (none of the three existing sealed routes do), which spends further oracle budget on a campaign that has already run r454-r478. Still open, independent: Piste B (commit the stabilized native backlog r433-r478) and Piste C (HUD guard-rail) from the approved plan.
